reply.summary: Researched ADR-004 (mirror src/ hierarchy in tools/orchestration/tests) and wrote docs/designs/004-mirror-src-hierarchy-in-tests/01-research.md. All of the ADR's load-bearing toolchain claims verified: tsconfig excludes tests/, no vitest config exists so the recursive default include discovers nested tests, gates.ts TEST_PATH_RE already matches nested paths, and all 26 test files only import ../src/... (never each other), so the move is git mv plus a uniform import-depth rewrite. Applied the prior-art and platform-notes lenses (Maven mirroring, Go colocation, Rust tests/; vitest 5 discovery+filtering, tsconfig, git rename detection). Flagged for the designer: the ADR says src/pipeline has 14 modules but it has 13; the 'import depth only' rule strands a stale path comment in pipeline-parallel-escalation.test.ts:45; and the flat tests/*.test.ts convention appears in two skill files (repo-practices:21 and test-strategy:27), not just the one the ADR names.
reply.commitMessage: docs: add research artifact for ADR-004 test-tree mirroring
docs: add design proposal for ADR-004 mirrored test tree

findings.location: Compatibility matrix — "Windows (case-insensitive checkout) | Expected — assumption | Same basis as macOS (A16)" with Assumption A7 "`TEST_PATH_RE = /(^|\/)tests\/|\.test\.ts$/` already matches nested `tests/…/x.test.ts` paths, so path gates are unchanged"
findings.problem: The only platform dimension justified for the macOS/Windows rows is filename case (A16). The dimension this move actually changes is path separators: nesting adds a second separator between `tests/` and the filename, and the quoted gate regex anchors the `tests/` tier with a literal forward slash. A7 is marked verified on the strength of reading the regex and a POSIX-style path form; nothing in the design establishes which separator form the pipeline feeds that regex, and the Windows row's Notes cover only git rename behavior (A15) and case (A16). Checklist item 6 (separators handled by a library, not string concatenation) is therefore unevaluated for the nested layout.
findings.fix: Add one clause to A7's Basis naming the separator form reaching `TEST_PATH_RE` (e.g. "paths reach the gate in POSIX form — git and vitest report `/`-separated paths") and carry it into the Windows row's Notes so the row answers separators and not only case. If the pipeline builds OS-native paths instead, downgrade that row and name the normalization step. The `.test\.ts$` alternation keeps file classification separator-safe, so exposure is limited to gates keying off the `tests/` prefix.

findings.location: Test strategy #3 — "`vitest run tests/pipeline` selects exactly the 23 moved files and none of the 3 root-tier tests (A6)" together with #7 "macOS/Windows rely on the A16 inference"
findings.problem: The one acceptance check whose meaning depends on the new nesting is a command embedding a forward slash in its filter string, and #7 excludes it from execution on every platform but Linux. On the two matrix rows describing case-insensitive (Windows-family) checkouts, the behavior of that nesting-specific filter is never established: the count assertion makes a mismatch fail rather than pass silently, but it would fail as an artifact of the check's platform, not of the move.
findings.fix: Add a one-line separator note to #3 — "filter string is matched against `/`-separated paths; verified on Linux" — so the platform boundary of the acceptance command is stated rather than implied by #7.

findings.location: Compatibility matrix, Node row — "discovery/compile behavior verified at these pinned majors (A4, A5; package.json:31,41,43)"
findings.problem: The cited dependencies are caret ranges (`vitest ^5.0.5`, `typescript ^6.0.3`), not pins, and A5 records that no `vitest.config.*` exists, so discovery is not held to the version that was actually checked. "Pinned majors" overstates the guarantee the matrix row rests on.
findings.fix: Reword to "verified against the vitest 5.x / TypeScript 6.x versions in the lockfile; discovery relies on vitest's default recursive `include`, which the design does not pin".

findings.location: Goals (bullet 3) and Chosen design ¶2 — "The only content change inside a moved file is its import depth, plus one stated carve-out (Decision, bullet 2…)" / "Content edit (Decision, bullet 2 + carve-out)."
findings.problem: The carve-out is attributed to ADR-004 Decision bullet 2, but that bullet as written states "The only content change permitted is the import depth (`../src/...` -> `../../src/...`)" — it forbids any other content change. The ADR (status: proposed) is left unamended; the Deferred section defers only the "14 modules" Context fix and nothing tasks an ADR amendment. So the design contradicts its source document as written: the single Rollout-2 commit contains a content change the Decision forbids, and the Risks-table acceptance check ("the diff contains only renames, import-depth lines, and that one comment line") enforces a rule the accepted Decision does not contain. The carve-out's substance is sound — A14's comment site at pipeline-parallel-escalation.test.ts:45 is verified (and a repo-wide grep for `tests/pipeline-` in tools/orchestration confirms it is the only real one, refuting the ADR Context's claim that tests never reference each other's paths) — but the deviation is unsanctioned while presented as Decision-compliant.
findings.fix: Amend ADR-004 Decision bullet 2 with one clause replacing the strict prohibition's scope: add "the single exception: a path-reference comment naming a file this move relocates is updated to its new path in the same commit" — then the proposal's "(Decision, bullet 2)" citations are accurate. Alternatively, keep the ADR text untouched and reword the proposal to record the carve-out as an explicit, tasked deviation from Decision bullet 2 rather than citing the Decision as its authority.

findings.location: Test strategy #4 (with Chosen design ¶3) — "pass unmodified, demonstrating `TEST_PATH_RE` and ownership checks treat nested paths identically"
findings.problem: The acceptance evidence cannot support the security-relevant half of the claim. The test-path gate and the ownership check are the privilege boundary deciding which files count as tests and which stage may edit them; the design's case that nesting does not move that boundary is one quoted regex (A7, TEST_PATH_RE only) plus these tests passing. But A14 states those tests' path strings are fixtures ("other in-test path mentions are inert fixture data") and Deferred keeps them in the old flat form ("Refreshing fixture path strings that mimic the old naming (e.g. `pipeline-lane.test.ts` at `pipeline-independence.test.ts:145`)"), so after the move the tests receive byte-identical inputs and a green run proves nothing about nested-path classification. No assumption row enumerates any path pattern other than TEST_PATH_RE (A8 is import specifiers, A11–A13 are agent globs and prompt prose), so a matcher keyed to the flat `pipeline-*` filename form could stop matching silently while `npm run check` stays green — fail open.
findings.fix: Replace the demonstrative claim in #4 with an assertion over a real nested path (classify the moved file's own path, e.g. tools/orchestration/tests/pipeline/gates.test.ts, through the same gate and ownership call sites A7 cites), and add one assumption row recording the static enumeration of every path pattern/literal in the gate and ownership code checked against the nested form. Fixture refresh stays deferred; the claim must not depend on it.

findings.location: Chosen design ¶3 — "No config change (Decision, bullet 3)"
findings.problem: The document has no trust-boundary statement anywhere, so checklist items 1, 2 and 4 are not evaluable: nothing classifies the inputs the change moves or leaves in place (repo files the pipeline reads, git metadata, agent permission grants), nothing states that no untrusted data is parsed, and nothing states that nothing leaves the machine. A later reader cannot tell whether the design considered that the paths it relocates are exactly the paths a gate and an agent grant match against.
findings.fix: Add one line to ¶3 (or Non-goals): the change moves only repo-local, trusted files; no untrusted/network/shared-binding input is parsed; the only security-relevant consumers of the moved paths are the in-repo path gate and the test-engineer agent's existing `**/tests/**` grant, both unchanged in scope before and after.

findings.location: Chosen design ¶2 / Rollout 2 — "rewrite every `../src/...` specifier to `../../src/...` (A8)"
findings.problem: The rewrite mechanism is unspecified and the evidence behind it is narrower than the instruction. A8's basis is an import-scoped grep (`from ['"]\.\.?/`), which says nothing about `../src/`-shaped substrings inside fixture path strings — exactly what A14 and Deferred confirm the gate and ownership tests contain. A content-wide substring rewrite can alter gate test inputs while `npm run check` stays green; the only guard offered is the manual diff read in Risk row 3.
findings.fix: State the rewrite as specifier-scoped using the same pattern A8 greps (`from '../src/...`), naming the substring substitution it replaces, and extend the Test strategy ¶1 diff check to assert no line outside import specifiers and the one carve-out comment changed.

findings.location: Rollout 1 — "Confirm no orchestration run is mid-branch against `tools/orchestration/tests/`"
findings.problem: The pre-condition that keeps the tree from ending up half-mirrored is a human confirmation with no mechanical check, and A18 marks it unverified ("must be checked at rollout"). If it slips, the tree carries renames plus newly authored old-form files: a partially applied move, which the path gate and ownership check classify inconsistently, and neither Test strategy #2 nor #3 detects it since both only compare expected file counts.
findings.fix: Add a fail-closed post-condition instead of relying on the human check: one static Test strategy item asserting grep finds zero remaining `tests/pipeline-*.test.ts` paths under tools/orchestration/tests/ after the commit.

findings.location: Test strategy #1–#2 — "with the same total test count as the pre-move baseline" / Rollout 3 — "Verify Test strategy items 1–6 locally before pushing; the reported file/test counts are the acceptance evidence"
findings.problem: The acceptance evidence is a count comparison with no baseline in any input and no step that captures one before it disappears. The research baseline the design cites records only file counts (26 = 23 + 3) and 65 import specifiers; no total test/assertion count appears in 01-research.md, the ADR, or the proposal, so Test strategy #1's "assertion counts per file are identical before and after the move" and #2's "same total test count" have no number to compare against. The ordering compounds it: Rollout 2 lands the commit (`git mv` ×23) and Rollout 3 only then verifies, so the flat tree is off disk when the comparison is specified. This is the one gap between the design's expected numbers and the research baseline that the text does not explain (performance checklist #6). Fix: add the pre-move count capture as Rollout step 0, before the moves.
findings.fix: Insert Rollout step 0 before the moves: run `npm run check` at the pre-move commit and record the reporter's file and test totals (and per-file counts if Test strategy #1 is kept) as the named baseline in the artifact the rollout already designates as evidence; then point Test strategy #1/#2 and the Risks "pre-move baseline" cell at that recorded run instead of an unstated number. This also cuts verification cost: one pre-move and one post-move `npm run check` together satisfy items 1, 2, 4 and 5, replacing the four-plus suite invocations the strategy currently implies.

findings.location: Chosen design ¶4 — "amends both convention surfaces that encode the old flat form ... to the recursive form `tests/**/*.test.ts` plus this rule"
findings.problem: Read literally, the full naming rule is written into both skill files, so two live instruction surfaces carry a copy of the rule after landing, inviting drift; the design's own "stated once" intent is not kept system-wide.
findings.fix: State the rule once: put it in repo-practices' existing "## Tests" section, and in test-strategy amend only the glob it restates (`tests/*.test.ts` → `tests/**/*.test.ts`), matching that line's existing "Follow `repo-practices` conventions:" pointer style. The flat form is still removed from both files, so Test strategy #6's grep still passes.

reply.summary: All five open findings consumed by changing the design, not padding it (206 lines before, 206 after). Correctness major (carve-out cited to ADR Decision bullet 2, which forbids it): the carve-out sub-system's 'carve-out' framing is deleted everywhere and recited instead as an explicit deviation, with the move commit tasked to amend bullet 2 by one clause (Chosen design ¶2, Goals bullet 3, Rollout 2, Deferred now states that only bullet 2 is edited while the Context '14 modules' deferral stands; the Options paragraph that argued for the carve-out was shortened to point at ¶2). Security major (fixture replay proves nothing about nested classification): Test strategy #4's demonstrative claim is replaced by assertions over the real moved path tools/orchestration/tests/pipeline/gates.test.ts through stagePathAllowed, landed in a separate test-only pre-move commit so the move commit stays mechanical, and A19 records the verified static enumeration showing TEST_PATH_RE (gates.ts:253 → gates.ts:262, runner.ts:232, runner.ts:1031) is the only test-path classifier in the gate/ownership code. Security minor (no trust boundary): one sentence in ¶3 — only trusted repo-local files move, nothing parses untrusted/network input, and the gate and the **/tests/** grant keep the same scope. Security minor (unspecified rewrite scope): ¶2 and Rollout 2 now bind the edit to A8's from '../src/... specifiers and name the content-wide substring substitution it forbids; Test strategy #1 and Risks row 3 bound the resulting diff. Security minor (in-flight-run pre-condition unguarded): Test strategy #2 carries the fail-closed post-condition — a grep finding zero leftover pipeline-*.test.ts paths after the commit — cited from Risks row 1. Net-zero achieved by deleting the duplicated Context scope restatement, three Goals/Non-goals bullets that restated the Decision or Deferred, two ¶4 sentences repeating the ADR's naming rule, and Rollout 4's restatement; the Revision log is rewritten in place as five section-anchored entries, one per still-material finding, superseding the prior r1 entry.
reply.commitMessage: docs: address r1 design review findings in 004 proposal

findings.location: Test strategy #2 — "fails closed on a half-applied move: a grep over `tools/orchestration/tests/` finds zero leftover `pipeline-*.test.ts` paths"
findings.problem: [new] The same document guarantees this grep matches. A14 ("other in-test path mentions are inert fixture data", citing `pipeline-independence.test.ts:145` and `pipeline-gates.test.ts:298-303`) and Deferred ("Refreshing fixture path strings that mimic the old naming (e.g. `pipeline-lane.test.ts` at `pipeline-independence.test.ts:145`) … no follow-up") both state that `pipeline-*.test.ts`-shaped strings remain inside files under that directory after a fully applied move. So a content grep for that pattern can never report zero: the rollout's step-3 verification of items 1–6 either can never pass, or is made to pass by loosening the pattern — which is exactly how a half-mirrored tree, i.e. a partially applied move with inconsistent path-gate classification, slips past the only mechanical guard added for it (checklist item 7). Fix: replace the content grep with a name-level filesystem check the deferred fixture strings cannot satisfy — `find tools/orchestration/tests -name 'pipeline-*.test.ts'` prints nothing — or keep the grep only when anchored to the path shape `tests/pipeline-` and applied to a file listing rather than to file contents.

findings.location: Test strategy #4 — "the existing `stagePathAllowed` block in the gate suite asserts the real post-move path `tools/orchestration/tests/pipeline/gates.test.ts`"
findings.problem: [re-raised, partially closed] The new assertion exercises the first of the two consumers A19 enumerates of the single `TEST_PATH_RE` ("`stagePathAllowed` (`gates.ts:262`, enforced at `runner.ts:232`) and the revert check (`runner.ts:1031`)"), so the revert check's nested-path behavior is still carried only by A7's regex argument rather than by an assertion. Fix: add one expectation over the same nested path at the revert-check call site in the same block, or add one A19 clause stating the revert check shares that one regex and therefore the same classification.

findings.location: Test strategy (intro + item 1) vs Rollout 1 — "the move is proven by the existing suite being unchanged, plus the one added assertion block in item 4" / "every previously existing test still exists and passes unmodified — assertion counts per file are identical before and after the move, and the moved files' diff contains only ¶2's allowed set"
findings.problem: Rollout 1 now lands a test-only commit before the move that adds assertions to the gate suite, tests/pipeline-gates.test.ts (existing describe('stagePathAllowed') block at pipeline-gates.test.ts:294-313) — one of the 23 files the move relocates. Against the branch's pre-work state, item 1's three invariants are all false for that file: the suite is not unchanged (the intro admits it), its per-file assertion count differs, and its diff across the two commits contains an assertion block that is neither an import line nor the comment line. Risks row 4 ("compares the vitest reporter's file/test counts to a pre-move baseline") inherits the same undefined baseline, and item 2's "with the pre-move test count" fails outright if the added block is a new case rather than extra expects. The baseline is never defined, so the acceptance evidence for Rollout 3 cannot be produced as written.
findings.fix: Name the baseline once: "before the move" = the move commit's parent (i.e. after the Rollout-1 test-only commit), and record the single expected delta — pipeline-gates.test.ts gains assertions inside the existing stagePathAllowed block while its test count and the 26-file count stay unchanged. Amends Test strategy #1 and Risks row 4's "pre-move baseline" rather than adding a new check.

findings.location: Goals/Non-goals bullet 2 + Chosen design ¶2 vs Rollout 1 — "Inside the move commit: no change to test logic, test names, fixtures, or file splits — 26 test files before, 26 after (Decision, bullet 2)"
findings.problem: The revision adopts the strict reading of ADR-004 Decision bullet 2 ("Bullet 2 permits import depth alone") to justify amending it for one comment line, then silently narrows the same bullet to "inside the move commit" in order to admit a test-logic change — item 4's added assertions — that bullet 2's own text forbids ("The only content change permitted is the import depth … No test logic, test names, fixtures, or file splits", ADR:42-44) and that ADR Consequences:78 makes an acceptance gate ("gate is `npm run check` green with an unchanged test count"). The comment deviation is declared and tasked to an amendment; this deviation from the same clause is neither, so the document reads bullet 2 two different ways.
findings.fix: State one reading: add a sentence to Rollout 1 (or Deferred) that bullet 2 constrains the move commit's diff only, that the Rollout-1 commit is a separate test change outside ADR-004's subject, and that it leaves test and file counts unchanged — or fold it into the same one-clause amendment to bullet 2.

findings.location: Test strategy item 2 + Risks row 1 — "fails closed on a half-applied move: a grep over `tools/orchestration/tests/` finds zero leftover `pipeline-*.test.ts` paths"
findings.problem: Read as written (item 6's "grep over" means a content grep), the check cannot pass: tools/orchestration/tests/pipeline-independence.test.ts:145 carries the fixture string `tools/orchestration/tests/pipeline-lane.test.ts`, which matches `pipeline-*.test.ts` and which the document deliberately keeps (Deferred: "Refreshing fixture path strings that mimic the old naming … no follow-up yet"). Verified: that line and pipeline-parallel-escalation.test.ts:45 are the only two occurrences of that shape in the tests directory. So the new fail-closed check either fails spuriously or pushes the implementer into the fixture edit the Deferred section defers — and Risks row 1's mitigation for the half-mirrored-tree risk rests on it. The deferral itself matches ADR-004 and is not re-opened; the new check contradicts the deferral.
findings.fix: Make item 2 filename-level: "a file listing over `tools/orchestration/tests/` (e.g. `git ls-files`) finds zero files named `pipeline-*.test.ts`", with a note that in-file fixture strings are excluded by Deferred. Same single sentence carries Risks row 1.

findings.location: Chosen design ¶1 — "The move is one commit in `tools/orchestration/` with no config change, in four parts"
findings.problem: The commit that section tasks is not confined to tools/orchestration/: Rollout 2 also commits the two skill-file amendments (.opencode/skills/repo-practices/SKILL.md:21 and .opencode/skills/test-strategy/SKILL.md:27) and, newly, the ADR-004 Decision bullet 2 amendment in docs/adrs/. The path qualifier contradicts the tasked content.
findings.fix: Drop the qualifier or name the areas: "one commit touching tools/orchestration/, the two skill files, and ADR-004 Decision bullet 2; no config change".

findings.location: Chosen design ¶2 — "never a content-wide `../src/` substring substitution, which would also rewrite the fixture path strings fed to the gate (A14)"
findings.problem: The stated hazard does not exist in the repo: the gate's fixture strings are `tools/orchestration/tests/…` and `docs/…` paths (pipeline-gates.test.ts:296-313, pipeline-independence.test.ts:145) and none contains `../src/`. Meanwhile the real hole in a `from '../src/`-keyed rewrite goes unmentioned — non-import relative specifiers, `vi.mock('../src/opencode-runner.js', …)` and `importOriginal<typeof import('../src/opencode-runner.js')>()` at cli.test.ts:29-30, the only two `../src/` sites beyond A8's 65, which that pattern skips. It is harmless today only because cli.test.ts is root-tier and does not move, a fact the design never states.
findings.fix: Replace the unsupported clause with the checked fact: "no moved file contains a relative specifier outside A8's 65 — the only such sites are the vi.mock and type-import in cli.test.ts, which stays at the package-root tier"; optionally add that fact to A8's basis.

reply.summary: All five open findings consumed by narrowing, not adding. (1) Baseline: Test strategy #1/#2 and Risks 4 no longer say 'before/after the move' or 'pre-move test count' — Rollout 1 now names the baseline once (the move commit's parent, after the test-only commit, with test and file counts unchanged) and the other sections cite it; #1's false 'assertion counts per file identical' clause is deleted. (2) Bullet-2 scope: the Non-goals bullet is rewritten to state the one reading — bullet 2 constrains the move commit's diff only and Rollout 1's added assertions are a separate test change outside ADR-004's subject, leaving both counts unchanged — so the strict-then-loose double reading cannot arise. (3) Fail-closed check: #2 is now a filename-level listing (`git ls-files`) rather than a content grep, and the Deferred fixture bullet records that those strings are outside that listing. (4) Chosen design ¶1 drops the false 'in `tools/orchestration/`' path qualifier; the areas are named once in Rollout 2. (5) ¶2's unhazardous 'content-wide `../src/` substitution' warning is deleted and replaced with the checked fact that no moved file holds a relative specifier outside A8's 65 (the only other `../src/` sites are `cli.test.ts:29-30`, which stays root-tier), with A8's row re-verified as 65 `from` matches vs 67 total `../src/`. Offsetting deletions in Options considered and Rollout 2 hold the document at 205 lines, one line shorter than before.
reply.commitMessage: docs: fix proposal baseline, bullet-2 scope, and flat-name check

findings.location: Chosen design ¶2 (with Assumption register A8, Test strategy #1, Rollout 2) — "no moved file holds a relative specifier outside those 65, and the only other `../src/` sites are the `vi.mock` and type-import in `cli.test.ts:29-30`, which stays at the package-root tier"
findings.problem: new — The newly added completeness claim is false, and it hides the one site class the move actually breaks. grep `\.\./ ` over tools/orchestration/tests/ finds 87 matches, not 67: the 65 from-imports (62 of them in moved files) + 2 cli.test.ts non-import `../src/` sites + 16 `new URL('<rel>', import.meta.url)` specifiers in 12 moved files — `'../prompts'`/`'../prompts/'` at pipeline-fix-trigger.test.ts:8, pipeline-prompts.test.ts:21, pipeline-budget.test.ts:85, pipeline-reply-contract.test.ts:83, pipeline-stage-lifecycle.test.ts:108, pipeline-funnel.test.ts:187, pipeline-proposal-size.test.ts:191, pipeline-parallel-integration.test.ts:191, pipeline-pass-finalize.test.ts:192, pipeline-parallel-fanout.test.ts:199, pipeline-parallel-escalation.test.ts:203 — plus `'../../../.opencode/skills/…'` at pipeline-prompts.test.ts:213,251,261,274,297 — + 4 inert `'../escape'` fixture strings (pipeline-identity.test.ts:65,68,103; pipeline-state-store.test.ts:156). new URL resolves against the moved file's own location, so one tier deeper turns `../prompts` into `tests/prompts` (absent) and `../../../.opencode/…` into `tools/.opencode/…` (absent), and these are live disk-read paths: loadTemplate is readFile(join(promptsDir, name)) at prompts.ts:26-27; pipeline-fix-trigger.test.ts:60 reads fix-tests.md through its PROMPTS_DIR; pipeline-prompts.test.ts:212-215 reads the skill files directly; the other nine suites feed that promptsDir into executeStage/resumePipeline, which render stage templates from disk. As written, the design rewrites only A8's 65 imports plus one comment line, and Test strategy #1 bounds the moved-file diff to exactly that allowed set — the ENOENT breakage is neither tasked nor permitted, `npm run check` cannot be green after the move, and ADR Decision bullet 2 ("the only content change permitted is the import depth") forbids the repair. The A8 row itself is narrowly true about imports and `../src/`, but its two cited greps structurally cannot see the URL sites, so it cannot support ¶2's claim; the 65 also span all 26 files (62 in moved files), so "the 65" is not the in-moved-file rewrite count either.
findings.fix: One coherent amendment: extend ¶2's rewrite set, Test strategy #1's allowed diff set, and Rollout 2's move-commit contents to the 16 depth-sensitive `new URL(..., import.meta.url)` sites (`'../prompts'` → `'../../prompts'`, `'../../../.opencode/...'` → `'../../../../.opencode/...'`), recite them in the bullet-2 amendment alongside the comment clause (replacing the current comment-only clause with e.g. "a relative path reference — code or comment — naming a location this move passes takes its new depth"), and replace ¶2's clause and A8's basis with the checked enumeration: grep `\.\./` = 87 sites = 65 from-imports (62 in moved files) + 2 cli.test.ts non-import `../src/` sites + 16 `new URL` sites + 4 inert `'../escape'` fixture strings. This replaces the false sentence rather than adding a new check; all five of my r1 findings are otherwise closed for real.

reply.summary: The r1c2 blocker (¶2's false completeness claim omitting 16 depth-sensitive `new URL('<rel>', import.meta.url)` sites — verified in-repo: 87 `../` sites = 65 from-imports (62 in moved files) + 2 cli.test.ts sites + 16 URL sites in 11 files + 4 inert '../escape' strings) is consumed by redefining ¶2's rewrite set to every depth-sensitive `../` reference (imports plus `../prompts/`→`../../prompts/` and `../../../.opencode/…`→`../../../../.opencode/…`), re-basing A8 on grep `\\.\./` (87 matches, four enumerated classes), folding the fix into the single bullet-2 amendment clause ('a relative path reference — code or comment — naming a location this move passes takes its new depth'), and propagating via rewrite (not addition) through Test strategy #1's allowed-diff set, Rollout 2's commit contents, Risks 3, Goals, A15, and Non-goals ('fixture inputs'); the Revision log's stale ¶2 entry is replaced in place. Diff is line-count neutral (205→205): every edit replaces text in situ.
reply.commitMessage: docs: revise 004 proposal to cover import.meta.url-relative path sites

findings.location: Chosen design ¶2 — "`../prompts/` → `../../prompts/`"
findings.problem: new — The mapping as written covers 15 of the 16 URL sites: pipeline-fix-trigger.test.ts:8 uses `new URL('../prompts', import.meta.url)` with no trailing slash, so a rewrite keyed to the quoted pattern leaves one site one tier shallow. Test strategy #1 only asserts the moved-file diff stays inside the allowed set, so it cannot catch a missed site; only the acceptance run (item 5) would.
findings.fix: Key the rewrite to the call rather than the string literal — "each `new URL('<rel>', import.meta.url)` in a moved file gains one `../`" — keeping the two mappings as examples instead of the operative pattern.

findings.location: Chosen design ¶2 (clause written into ADR bullet 2) — "a relative path reference — code or comment — naming a location this move passes takes its new depth"
findings.problem: new — At the edge this revision closed, the clause reads wide enough to cover A8's fourth class: the 4 `'../escape'` strings are relative path references in code (verified inert: pipeline-state-store.test.ts:156 writes them into a mkdtemp checkpoint; pipeline-identity.test.ts:65,68,103 feed them to sanitizeSlug/deriveIdentity), and Deferred deliberately keeps other in-test path strings stale. The exclusion currently rests only on A8's word "inert", so the durable ADR sentence and the proposal's closed enumeration can be read against each other at implementation time.
findings.fix: Qualify the clause by resolution rather than by label: "a path reference that the moved file resolves against its own location — code or comment — takes its new location", which excludes the escape strings and A14's inert fixtures by definition instead of by an appended label.

findings.location: Chosen design ¶2 — "takes its new depth" with "(the comment site: A14)"
findings.problem: new — The comment A14 names is `tests/pipeline-reply-contract.test.ts` at pipeline-parallel-escalation.test.ts:45 (verified verbatim). It carries no `../`, so it is not inside A8's 87-site enumeration, and its edit is a directory insertion plus prefix drop, not a depth change. r1's clause ("takes its new path") sanctioned that edit; the replacement clause's "new depth" does not describe it, so the comment line is covered only by the parenthetical while the ADR sentence is what a reviewer of the commit checks.
findings.fix: One word in the clause — "takes its new location" — and in ¶2 name the actual edit ("the comment's path gains the `pipeline/` tier and drops the prefix: A14"), replacing the current verb rather than adding a new caveat.

findings.location: Chosen design ¶2 — "`../prompts/` → `../../prompts/`"
findings.problem: new — The mapping as written covers 15 of the 16 URL sites: pipeline-fix-trigger.test.ts:8 uses `new URL('../prompts', import.meta.url)` with no trailing slash, so a rewrite keyed to the quoted pattern leaves one site one tier shallow. Test strategy #1 only asserts the moved-file diff stays inside the allowed set, so it cannot catch a missed site; only the acceptance run (item 5) would.
findings.fix: Key the rewrite to the call rather than the string literal — "each `new URL('<rel>', import.meta.url)` in a moved file gains one `../`" — keeping the two mappings as examples instead of the operative pattern.

findings.location: Chosen design ¶2 (clause written into ADR bullet 2) — "a relative path reference — code or comment — naming a location this move passes takes its new depth"
findings.problem: new — At the edge this revision closed, the clause reads wide enough to cover A8's fourth class: the 4 `'../escape'` strings are relative path references in code (verified inert: pipeline-state-store.test.ts:156 writes them into a mkdtemp checkpoint; pipeline-identity.test.ts:65,68,103 feed them to sanitizeSlug/deriveIdentity), and Deferred deliberately keeps other in-test path strings stale. The exclusion currently rests only on A8's word "inert", so the durable ADR sentence and the proposal's closed enumeration can be read against each other at implementation time.
findings.fix: Qualify the clause by resolution rather than by label: "a path reference that the moved file resolves against its own location — code or comment — takes its new location", which excludes the escape strings and A14's inert fixtures by definition instead of by an appended label.

findings.location: Chosen design ¶2 — "takes its new depth" with "(the comment site: A14)"

findings.location: Chosen design ¶2 — "the 16 `new URL('<rel>', import.meta.url)` paths — `../prompts/` → `../../prompts/`, `../../../.opencode/…` → `../../../../.opencode/…`" (with A8's "16 depth-sensitive `new URL('<rel>', import.meta.url)` paths in 11 moved files" and Test strategy #1's "depth-adjusted `new URL` lines")
findings.problem: The revision moved 16 runtime path resolutions from untouched into the move's diff. At r1 the only edited path strings were import specifiers, resolved by the toolchain; these 16 resolve at run time against the moved file's own location, and Test strategy #7 ("Linux executes items 1–5") means no non-Linux run ever exercises the new depth. The macOS/Windows rows still justify "Expected — assumption" solely with case (A16) and git rename (A15), neither of which speaks to these sites, and the design never states how the URL becomes a path: a `URL` handed to `fs`/`fileURLToPath` is `/`-separated and platform-safe, while a `.pathname` read or a string-joined path on a case-insensitive checkout surfaces as ENOENT only for a maintainer off Linux. Checklist item 6 (separators handled by a library, not string editing) is unevaluated for the widened scope.

findings.location: Chosen design ¶2 — "a relative path reference — code or comment — naming a location this move passes takes its new depth"
findings.problem: This clause is the new permanent rule the move commit writes into ADR-004 Decision bullet 2 (Deferred bullet 3, Rollout 2), but it keys on the target being "a location this move passes". Replaces the existing sentence; adds nothing.
